recipes.name: Classic Meatloaf
ingredients_raw: 0.5 medium red bell pepper, coarsely chopped
1 teaspoon Sriracha sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Line a baking dish with lightly greased foil.
Place carrot, celery, onion, bell pepper, mushrooms, and garlic in a food processor; pulse until very finely chopped, almost to a purée. Transfer to a large mixing bowl.

Add ground chuck to the vegetables, along with Worcestershire sauce, egg, Italian herbs, salt, black pepper, and cayenne. Mix gently with a wooden spoon until ingredients are just combined. Sprinkle in bread crumbs and gently mix with your fingertips until just combined; don't overmix.
Shape the mixture into a loaf, about 4 inches high by 6 inches across. Place in the prepared baking pan.
Bake in the preheated oven just until the meatloaf is hot, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir brown sugar, ketchup, Dijon, and Sriracha for glaze in a small bowl until brown sugar has dissolved.
Remove meatloaf from the oven. Spoon glaze on the top of the meatloaf with the back of a spoon, then pull a tiny bit glaze down the sides.

Return to the oven, and bake until no longer pink inside, 45 to 75 more minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the loaf should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), so start checking at 45 minutes and continue baking until meatloaf reaches that temperature. Cooking time will depend on shape and thickness of the meatloaf.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's traditional meatloaf recipe uses classic ingredients like sautéed vegetables, spices, and bread crumbs. An old-fashioned glaze adds flavor to every slice.

video.description: Get ready to savor the comforting flavors of our Classic Meatloaf! This timeless dish is a culinary masterpiece that combines seasoned ground beef, onions, and breadcrumbs, baked to perfection. Each slice is tender, juicy, and bursting with rich, savory goodness. Topped with a tangy tomato glaze that adds the perfect touch of sweetness, this meatloaf will transport you back to your childhood. Whether you're enjoying it as a hearty family dinner or craving a nostalgic comfort food fix, our Classic Meatloaf is sure to hit the spot. Gather around the table and experience the taste of home with every bite.

review.reviewBody: I increased the italian herbs (I assumed that to mean italian seasoning--I used my own homemade italian seasoning) to two teaspoons and I used homemade croutons (day old bread, brushed with EVOO and garlic powder, cut into 1 inch pieces and baked until crispy, then cooled) that I ground down in the food processor. Those were the only changes I made. Ginormous meat loaf. It fit in my Perfect Meat Loaf pan, but just barely, with a quarter inch at the top. Mine did take almost two hours to bake, taken out the last half hour to pour over the glaze. This was one of the better meat loaves I've ever made. Very flavorful, quite filling. I served homemade biscuits and Cheesy Vegetable Medley with this. Out of that big meatloaf, just under half remains--my oldest boy ate two pieces and my husband ate three! We all really liked it. The rest will be used for sandwiches in lunches tomorrow. I'll make this meat loaf again.

Loved it! Moist and tasty. A keeper. I didn’t make the glaze since I had a mushroom gravy. I always add pork sausage for flavor but I don’t bake it in a loaf pan-too greasy! I use a broiler pan, lining the bottom tray with parchment and spray oil on the top tray. All the grease falls through the holes into the bottom and it is perfect! I top it off with a pinch of salt in top & a sprinkling of Italian seasoning before baking. Delish 💕

Delicious. I upped the amount of sriracha sauce so it was nice and spicey. Next time I won't put the beef mixture in aluminum foil. The juices made it difficult to remove the loaf from the pan. I also baked longer than the time specified.
Perfect. I sautéed my vegetables. I also made a panade with bread crumbs half and half and egg yolks. It made a very tender and flavorful loaf. I also cooked on a baking sheet with parchment paper

I used a beef pork blend because hubby bought it on accident and I was trying to use it up. I didn't have any fresh mushrooms and I'm certain that would have helped with flavor. I added a little liquid smoke but I'll add more next time. I'll also mince the carrots insted of chopping them because they didnt cook thoroughly. The glaze was amazing! It tasted better the next day and the heat from the cayenne came through more. I might just use a packet of Italian dressing mix rather than the Italian seasoning next time to up the flavor and add more garlic.

I make my meatloaf on a roasting pan so the drippings fall away from the meatloaf. Using a loaf pan will cause the meatloaf to sit in those drippings. Also, I like to use BBQ sauce on my meatloaf instead of the traditional ketchup. I just don't like a blob of ketchup on baked meat. No peppers or mushrooms, either.

I used what I had so the main difference was only 1.5 lbs beef and no mushroom. I substituted balsamic vinegar instead of Worcestershire. I grated the veggies on a cheese grater and they were perfect! This meatloaf was moist and full of flavor. I did 20+40 minutes in the oven. I used foil but next time I’ll use parchment paper as it still stuck to the foil even though I used olive oil to grease. Will definitely make this again!

I’ve been making meatloaf for years but like to change it up occasionally. The flavor of this meatloaf was great. Mincing the veggies in a processor made a huge difference in the moistness of the meat. I made recipe as written. The cayenne definitely kicked it up a notch. I also put a shot of hot sauce into the glaze. The spiciness of the meatloaf may be a turn-off to kids. 4 stars because the cooking time was off. After cooking for 55 minutes at 325 meat temperature was 116. Turned oven up to 350 and cooked for another 1/2 hour which brought it up to 160.

This meatloaf was delicious, though I didn't make the glaze because I had a request for mushroom sauce the night I made it. Next time I make it I will cut the garlic back to probably one clove, and I will saute the vegetable mixture before adding it to the meat, as the raw garlic and onion flavors were a bit too strong for us. Still devoured it happily, though!

Couldn’t have asked for a better tasting Meatloaf recipe. I’ve made this about six times now. Some times I almost purée the veggies in my Ninja Bullet, sometimes I just chop them small. Other than that, I make it exactly as written. After making it the first time, you can adjust seasonings to your liking. It always comes out amazing. Just the right amount of sweet and savory.

I used half of the portion and the meatloaf was very moist and tasty. I skipped white mushrooms. For the sauce, I forgot to put Worcestershire sauce in the meat mix so I used Dark Soy sauce for the sauce on top. The result was good. It was very easy to make. The instruction was very easy to follow. I'd make this again and probably use baby bella instead of white mushrooms. Thank you chef John.
Best meatloaf ever! I used ground turkey and just mixed in the cut up veggies because we like more texture, and it was amazing. I'll be making this weekly.
Great meatloaf. Made as written except for the mushrooms which I didn't have, The Sriracha glaze was really unique and tasty. Served with mashed potatoes and a chef salad

Authentic classic meatloaf was not just beef. As I recall my grandmother made it with Beef, Veal and Pork. Hence the name MEAT LOAF and not BEEF LOAF. It was the mid 70's and beyond when folks started getting lazy. :)

Too salty in my opinion, and not a good combination of flavors with the worcestershire etc. Would not make again, and I usually love Chef John recipes. I noticed the recipe was different than the video also - the video showed finely chopped vegetables while the recipe said "coarse chopped" which didn't make any sense in a meatloaf
I've made this meatloaf many times and my family loves it! The only thing different that I do is I double the glaze ingredients so that there's lots of yummy glaze on the top! Great recipe!!
I use cooked down (thickened) golden mushroom soup for the glaze
This dish was a hit with my family. Meatloaf was super flavorful and moist. 10/10
Easy, loaded with flavor, and great texture. There’s one, simple reason why John’s recipes always hit the top of my search results: it’s always the best.
I substituted Oatmeal for bread crumbs. I used a mixture of beef, veal and pork. Very good
